svg.title: CQRS
svg.desc: CQRS. Separate the write model (commands) from read models (queries), each optimised for its job. Step 1, Commands change state: PlaceOrder: the handler checks the rules, the write model commits, and the client gets 201 Created. Step 2, Project to read models: Change #7 flows to the projector, which updates each denormalised view: order summary and search. Step 3, Queries hit the read side: A query reads one ready-made table, with no joins, from read replicas that scale apart from writes. Step 4, Eventual consistency: Right after CancelOrder, a read still shows placed: the view lags until the projector catches up.

g.text: PlaceOrder: the handler checks the rules, the write model commits, and the client gets 201 Created.
Change #7 flows to the projector, which updates each denormalised view: order summary and search.
A query reads one ready-made table, with no joins, from read replicas that scale apart from writes.
Right after CancelOrder, a read still shows placed: the view lags until the projector catches up.
read model · one row per order
Commands are business tasks, not generic updates.
Rules run on normalised tables; one transaction commits the change.
One change, many views: each is shaped for one screen.
The checkpoint lets the projector resume where it left off after a restart.
One table, no joins. Reads usually far outnumber writes: scale them alone.
When a user must see their own write:
• return the new state in the command’s response
• version token: serve the read once the view has #8
• optimistic UI: show cancelled at once, confirm later
